phase: M6 Phase 5I-A - Ground-Truth Rebuild + Hindi Retrieval Determinism Forensic
status: FORENSIC COMPLETE - no production code changed
executive_summary: Objective A (trustworthy current-corpus evaluation foundation) succeeded: new 19-entry ground truth built from directly reading current canonical chunk text, live-verified at 84% top-5 hit rate (16/19), with the 3 misses themselves informative (script/cross-language divergence). Building it surfaced and corrected a real methodological error from Phase 5H: RetrievalResult.chunk_id is the payload-level chunk_id, not Qdrant's raw point id (a deterministic uuid5 hash of it). Re-verified correctly, Phase 5H's bottom-line conclusion (old ground truth unusable, 0/26 IDs present) still stands. Objective B (Hindi retrieval determinism) produced a clean, unexpected result: the retrieval pipeline is provably 100% deterministic across 90 repeated calls spanning 8 query/collection/mode combinations, zero variation at any stage. Further investigation found the original Phase 5H 'inconsistency' actually compared TWO DIFFERENT retrieval queries (Hindi vs English phrasing), not a repeated identical query - a mischaracterization in that report, now corrected. No production retrieval change is recommended or implemented.

canonical_corpus_state.architectural_finding: Every one of the 542 points' Qdrant point id differs from its own payload chunk_id field. Confirmed via direct code read (vector_store.py _point_id_for()): Qdrant point ID is a deterministic uuid5(fixed_namespace, chunk_id) hash of the logical chunk_id, separately stored in payload and returned by search_similar()/scroll_all_chunks() as RetrievalResult.chunk_id. Intentional, consistent, deterministic - not a bug - but an easy trap for external verification scripts querying the wrong field.

root_cause_analysis.actual_root_cause: The original Phase 5H observation itself was mischaracterized. Re-reading that phase's own script confirmed the two contrasting cases used DIFFERENT retrieval queries (Hindi 'स्टैक क्या है?' vs English 'What is a stack?'), not a repeated identical query. Phase 5H's report incorrectly characterized this as 'the identical query... called twice in one process, materially different candidate sets' - corrected here.
root_cause_analysis.true_explanation: Ordinary cross-language retrieval-quality variance (already-documented Phase 5E/5H phenomenon) between two different-language phrasings of a conceptually similar question - not a same-input-different-output bug
